answer: Geodetic latency attestation: an agent joins by solving timed challenge-responses with three fixed network anchors—raven, inlet, ridge—on distinct autonomous systems. Anchors measure round-trip delay and jitter; a verifier checks the vector against speed-of-light and routing bounds. Agents behind one host share delay signatures, so sybils need distinct physical sites with independent uplinks and calibrated clocks; forging N identities costs N colocations plus latency calibration, not just N keys.
